llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed business-lead search integration that uses a vendor API, may create a trial account after consent, and writes local reports and an API key file.

dimensions.detail: Network use is scoped to the vendor API/registration domains plus optional web search; local access is narrow, though auto-registration sends platform, CPU architecture, and a hashed MAC-derived identifier after consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Metadata declares the ZLBX_API_KEY environment variable, while the instructions also disclose reading ~/.zlbx/config.json, writing reports, and creating ~/.zlbx/config.json after auto-registration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation language is broad across leads, customer development, projects, and procurement opportunities, but it stays within the described opportunity-discovery domain and requires cost disclosure before scans.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists an API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json and HTML reports in ~/zlbx-opportunity-radar-files/, but it does not install background workers or automatically schedule recurring scans.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, API calls, ranking workflow, report generation, and vendor links fit a business opportunity radar; the zero-configuration trial account flow is sensitive but disclosed as part of using the vendor service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable sending opportunity search terms to Zhiliao Biaoxun, allowing an optional trial-account registration that sends platform, CPU architecture, and a hashed MAC-derived identifier after consent, and storing a returned API key and HTML reports under your home directory.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Confirmed local config read and report/key writes; these are narrow and disclosed in the artifact, though not fully represented in the top metadata.
[TP4] expected: The HTML report, embedded branding, export controls, and platform links are disclosed in SKILL.md, report-template.md, and render_report.py and align with a shareable vendor report.
[SDI-1] expected: Auto-registration creates a trial account only when no API key is available and auto-register.md requires user consent before collection or registration.
[SDI-2] expected: The platform, architecture, and hashed MAC flow is privacy-sensitive, but the artifact limits it to trial deduplication, avoids hostname/user/path collection, and requires consent before execution.
[SDI-2] expected: The quota-exhausted SID flow generates an auto-login recharge link for an auto-created account; it does not perform a recharge itself and is disclosed as a billing recovery path.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger scope is broad, but the examples and conditions remain tied to opportunity, lead, project, and procurement discovery, with a stated call budget and cost notice.
[SQP-2] expected: The 'no extra prompts' key lookup language is moderated by the referenced auto-register gate, which explicitly requires consent before device feature collection or registration.
[E1] expected: External JSON POSTs are expected for the vendor API and auto-registration; the sensitive registration fields are disclosed and limited rather than hidden exfiltration.
